one_line: Ayurvedic scholar-physician whose Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya shaped medical learning from northwest India to Tibet and Kerala.

appearance.age_look: late 40s, lean and slightly ascetic scholar’s build
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown northwestern Indian complexion, sharp thoughtful eyes with gently arched brows, short well-groomed beard and moustache, a small sandalwood tilak at the centre of the forehead, default expression calm and observant with a faint teaching smile
appearance.hair: dark brown-black hair, parted in the middle and combed back into a low, neatly tied bun at the nape held by a simple wooden pin; no turban, just a plain off-white cotton headband tied around the crown to keep hair back
appearance.costume: austere 6th–7th century scholar-physician attire: ankle-length unbleached off-white cotton dhoti wrapped snugly with clean folds and a deep maroon border, paired with a long-sleeved light beige cotton angarkha-style upper garment crossing left over right and tied with simple cloth ties, a soft maroon cotton uttariya draped from left shoulder across the chest and around the back like a shawl, plain leather sandals, minimal jewellery of a single small gold stud in each ear and a thin tulsi-bead mala around the neck; no royal ornaments, textiles mostly plain with very subtle woven stripes on the uttariya border
appearance.signature: a hand-sized palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya tied with a red cord, held in his left hand, with a simple wooden stylus tucked into the cord

ref_desc: Vāgbhaṭa appears as a lean late-40s scholar with oval medium-brown face, short beard, hair in a low bun and headband, in off-white dhoti, beige angarkha, maroon shawl and sandals, carrying a red-cord-tied palm-leaf Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya manuscript with stylus, in warm maroon-beige tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Vāgbhaṭa as a dignified 6th–7th century Ayurvedic scholar-physician: late-40s, lean build, oval medium-brown face, sharp eyes, short well-groomed beard and moustache, small sandalwood tilak, dark brown-black hair combed back into a low bun secured with a wooden pin and a plain off-white headband. He wears an ankle-length unbleached off-white cotton dhoti with a deep maroon border, a long-sleeved light beige cotton angarkha-style upper garment crossing left over right, and a soft maroon cotton uttariya shawl draped from his left shoulder across the chest and around his back. Add simple leather sandals, a thin tulsi-bead mala and tiny gold ear studs, with textiles mostly plain and only subtle woven stripes on the shawl border. In his left hand he holds a palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya tied with a red cord, with a simple wooden stylus tucked into the cord, posed calmly as if teaching, using a warm palette of off-white, maroon, light beige and deep brown so this design can be redrawn consistently across many panels.
